title: Apollo 17 VIP Site Anaglyph
summary: Get out your red/blue glasses and check out this stereo scene from Taurus-Littrow valley on the Moon! The color anaglyph features a detailed 3D view of Apollo 17's Lunar Rover in the foreground.

title: Researchers explore the use of AI and smart sensors to improve food safety quickly, affordably
summary: The smartJAN project, developed by the eVIDA research group at the University of Deusto in collaboration with Kernet and Fundación Miranda, has completed the development of a functional prototype capable of detecting the presence of LTPs (lipid transfer proteins), a family of plant proteins that includes allergens capable of triggering severe allergic reactions. These allergens are particularly relevant in the Mediterranean region.

title: Event Horizon Telescope views the dynamics and geometry of a black hole jet in extreme detail
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), a massive international collaboration of scientists and radio observatories, is like the gift that keeps on giving. In 2019, the EHT Collaboration gave us the first image of a black hole: the supermassive black hole (SMBH) at the heart of the M87 galaxy (M87*). In 2022, it provided the first image of Sagittarius A*, the SMBH at the center of the Milky Way. Between 2024 and 2026, the international array also produced detailed images of the relativistic jets emanating from 3C 84 and M87*.

title: Should space data centers run on solar panels, nuclear reactors or both?
summary: The last few days we've been covering a series of papers by Dr. Slava Turyshev of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory about the constraints surrounding the use of orbital data centers in space. One that has come up repeatedly is weight, and the solar panels used to power these data centers contribute a significant portion of that weight. So why not go with an alternative power source? Nuclear energy in space applications is having a bit of a moment currently—maybe it could provide the power needed for the orbital data center revolution?

title: New technologies help Natural History Museum uncover 92 species in its transformed gardens
summary: The Natural History Museum's transformed gardens in South Kensington are revealing new insights into London's urban wildlife. Among the 92 species recorded at the site for the first time between its reopening in July 2024 and the end of 2025 are the striking emperor moth and small red-eyed damselfly.

title: RNA discovery reveals how gut bacterium adapts to life in intestinal mucus
summary: The mucus layer in the human gut is a tough place for bacteria: nutrients are scarce, and conditions are harsh. How do bacteria adapt to such extreme environments? Researchers at the Helmholtz Institute for RNA-based Infection Research (HIRI) and the Chair of Microbiology of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität (JMU) in Würzburg, working with scientists at Vanderbilt Health in the United States, have identified a key regulator.

title: AI simulates electron hops over far longer times than conventional quantum calculations
summary: To predict how a material will behave, we need to know which atoms are located where. This allows us, for example, to explain whether a material is suitable as a catalyst for certain chemical reactions. But often, that is not enough: even if all the atoms stay exactly where they are, the distribution of electric charge within the material can change dramatically. Electrons can jump from one atom to another, changing the forces between atoms as well as the material's chemical reactivity.

title: Targeted conversion of carbon dioxide into chemical feedstocks: CO₂ helps shape its own catalyst
summary: Electrochemists at the University of Duisburg-Essen have discovered through computer simulations that carbon dioxide (CO₂) helps shape the surface of its own catalyst when the catalyst is restructured using voltage pulses. The calculations suggest that this allows CO₂ to be converted preferentially into formic acid. The findings have been published in Advanced Functional Materials.

title: Rocks under the lens: A simple microscope opens new possibilities for quantitative rock analysis
summary: Rocks hold a wealth of information about Earth's history. The size, shape and orientation of the mineral grains that make them up can reveal how rocks formed, deformed and changed deep beneath the surface. However, collecting this information has traditionally required specialized equipment and time-consuming analysis.

title: Lab experiments suggest bat RSV can enter human cells, but existing antibodies block it
summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe respiratory disease and is responsible for numerous deaths each year. A research team led by DZIF scientist Dr. Wendy K. Jo and DZIF scientist Dr. Jan Felix Drexler at Charité—University Medicine Berlin, as well as DZIF board member Dr. Thomas Pietschmann and Dr. Sibylle Haid from TWINCORE in Hanover, has now characterized a virus in West African fruit bats that is genetically distinct from known RSV variants but belongs to the same viral family as RSV.

title: Battery-free implant harvests ultrasound energy and glows to reveal its condition
summary: Implantable bioelectronics enable health care professionals to continuously monitor patients' physiological conditions, deliver targeted treatments and support recovery. However, once implanted, these devices are difficult to inspect directly, and damage or degradation may go undetected until complications occur. Limited battery lifetimes and leakage risks also raise safety concerns.

title: Work-life balance predicts job satisfaction more strongly than pay or flexible working in study
summary: Work-life balance has a stronger association with job satisfaction than pay or flexible working arrangements, according to a study of employees in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) published in the International Journal of Economics and Business Research.

title: New research establishes fundamental complexity limit for quantum circuit optimization
summary: Quantum circuit optimization is an important research area, as the computational resources required to execute quantum algorithms remain a major challenge. In particular, two-qubit operations are generally associated with higher error rates than single-qubit gates on current quantum hardware, making reducing the number of two-qubit gates an important objective.

title: Artemis III Astronaut Andre Douglas Visits VAB
summary: NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, Artemis III mission specialist, stands inside an RS-25 engine test article during a visit to the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026.

title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
summary: NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency.

title: The narwhal’s legendary “unicorn horn” holds a remarkable engineering secret
summary: The narwhal’s iconic spiral tusk, once prized in Europe as the horn of a mythical unicorn, conceals an extraordinary feat of natural engineering.

title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
summary: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil.

title: The Moon Watchers

summary: A cloud layer encircled the flanks of the volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula but left its restless summit caldera in view

title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
summary: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling.

title: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean
summary: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves.

title: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
summary: Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed.

title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
summary: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers.

title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China
